Subject: Request: feasibility for hybrid BAA + GLBA coverage for pilot

Hi Mateo,

Thanks again for the demo last week. MedFin and Hospital Systems are moving toward a small joint pilot (customer-facing billing reconciliation feature) that will involve both protected health information and consumer financial information. Legal asked me to check feasibility for a hybrid approach: Redwood to sign a BAA for PHI handling related to the hospital workflows, while also supporting GLBA contractual controls for the MedFin side.

High-level asks from our side:
- Can Redwood operate under a split-contract model (BAA for PHI flows, GLBA addendum for finance flows) while serving a single tenant/pilot instance?
- What evidence can you provide on residency, subprocessors, and encryption-in-transit and at-rest?
- Any objections to a short list of GLBA clause redlines (we'll attach)?

Timing: procurement would like an initial answer + evidence checklist by Sep 15 so internal counsel can draft an addendum. I attached a brief sample of the expected GLBA clauses and a one-page dataflow.

Thanks,
Lara Chen
Sr. Director, Privacy & Compliance
Hospital Systems

- High-level dataflow mapping for split-processing paths (we'll mark which requests are treated under BAA vs GLBA).

- Encryption attestation and SOC2 summary.

Vanessa / Soojin / Marcus — forwarding a request from Hospital Systems and MedFin. The ask: feasibility for a single-tenant pilot where PHI is handled under a BAA and consumer finance data under GLBA. Procurement needs an evidence checklist by 9/15.

Quick notes for the checklist (please reply inline):
- Residency/segmentation: customer prefers a single logical tenant. Options: Dedicated pool (recommended) or VPC private deployment. Does Dedicated allow per-route policy segregation so we can mark certain endpoints as BAA-covered?
- Subprocessors: need current list + plan for any onshore-only subprocessors for PHI portions.
- Crypto: provide TLS ciphers, KMS scheme, and attest to AES-256 at rest. See our attestation draft attached.
- SOC2: PR and infra summaries are fine, but counsel will ask for evidence of change management and key rotation cadence.
- Redlines: Legal will push on retention limits and re-use of model cache for PHI prompts (we need to confirm KV cache segmentation).

Attachments: redwood-encryption-attestation.txt

Can Security/Infra confirm whether dedicated pool + route-based policy is implementable for a short pilot (30–60 days)? Marcus, can you comment on cache isolation and quantization policy implications?

Thanks — I'll consolidate and send to Lara + Rajiv once we have a short checklist.
Mateo
